### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **51** documentable anchor(s).

**21** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d1663ba1826c338861c3b92c117346322a6af8fa`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `packageId (4 routes)`
- **11** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **153** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d1663ba1826c338861c3b92c117346322a6af8fa` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `682ada6a125a90973b1925604fabee4e0b8418cd` — the merge of head `12daab9542fa8ea76bdcce4d3650b7b6da5edcc2` into base `d1663ba1826c338861c3b92c117346322a6af8fa`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 682ada6a125a90973b1925604fabee4e0b8418cd && git checkout 682ada6a125a90973b1925604fabee4e0b8418cd
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d1663ba1826c338861c3b92c117346322a6af8fa 12daab9542fa8ea76bdcce4d3650b7b6da5edcc2 && git checkout -B drift-repro d1663ba1826c338861c3b92c117346322a6af8fa && git merge --no-ff 12daab9542fa8ea76bdcce4d3650b7b6da5edcc2

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d1663ba1826c338861c3b92c117346322a6af8fa
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d1663ba1826c338861c3b92c117346322a6af8fa` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `12daab9542fa8ea76bdcce4d3650b7b6da5edcc2`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts (the `reviewFace` hit, schema face), packages/metadata-core/src/protocol-handshake.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/protocol-handshake-dependencies.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-package-install.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-package-install-dependencies.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/packages-install-dependency-missing.test.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-dependency-missing.test.ts, scripts/adr-anchors/packages__metadata-core__src__protocol-handshake.ts.json, scripts/docs-audit/handwritten-docs.json + packages/spec/src/kernel/manifest.zod.ts (`ManifestSchema.dependencies`, `version`), packages/spec/src/system/app-install.zod.ts (`AppCompatibilityCheckSchema.issues[].category`, `AppManifestSchema`), packages/spec/src/marketplace/package-version.zod.ts (`PackageDependencySchema`), packages/spec/src/kernel/package-dependency-dual-source.test.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/errors.ts (`MetadataError`), packages/metadata-core/src/index.ts (`export *` of the handshake module), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (the two in-process `installPackage` callers), packages/core/src/artifact-packages.ts (`resolveArtifactPackageEntries`), scripts/check-adr-anchors.mjs, scripts/docs-audit/check-audit-scope.mjs, scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, packages/qa/dogfood/test/authz-probe-blind-spot.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/i18n.ts, .github/workflows/ci.yml (dogfood job conditions). The prose face (.changeset/25792-pre-install-dependency-check.md, content/docs/deployment/app-dependencies.mdx, content/docs/protocol/kernel/plugin-spec.mdx, the three regenerated reference pages, content/docs/deployment/meta.json) was read for the claims it makes about the code above.

### ① Derived judgments

**CI state at review time (2026-10-26T08:18Z, 46 check-runs on the head).** 32 concluded `success`, 0 `failure`. Still in progress: Test Core shards 1, 3, 4, 5 and 7 of 8, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check UI`. Concluded green and load-bearing here: `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, Test Core shards 2, 6, 8, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · docs & code guards` (runs `check:docs-audit-scope` and `check:error-status-conformance`), `Lint · repo & tooling gates` (runs `check:adr-anchors`), `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Spec property liveness`, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Part-of PR must not also close its card`, `Check PR Size`. The judgments below are rendered on what has concluded; the five open Test Core shards and the workspace typecheck are the only gates still owed, and nothing in the diff was found that predicts them red.

**A. The accept set at the three install acts — right.** The one predicate `checkDeclaredDependencies` (protocol-handshake.ts) is called from exactly three places and nowhere else in the diff: `installPackage` in protocol-package-install.ts through `assertDeclaredDependencies`, placed after `assertProtocolCompat` and before the `prior` read, the registry write and the persist, so the composed arm of `POST /api/v1/packages` and the two in-process callers in protocol.ts (`duplicatePackage` at the `dupManifest` call and the base-package plan) inherit it; the no-protocol fallback arm of `POST /api/v1/packages` (packages.ts) directly after its own `assertProtocolCompat` and before `registry.installPackage`; and `POST /api/v1/marketplace/install-local` at step 1c', after the id gate and the handshake and before the install-mode gate and the manifest service, on both branches (the inline manifest and the cloud snapshot converge at `manifest` before 1b). Not touched: the `kernel:ready` rehydrate in the install-local plugin, `packages/services/service-package` (the `sys_packages` rehydrate), `PATCH /api/v1/packages/:id` (`updatePackage`). The cloud-connection test pins that a ledger entry whose dependency is absent at boot still re-registers.

Refused `422 DEPENDENCY_MISSING` after this PR: a delivered package whose own `manifest.dependencies` record carries an entry whose id is neither delivered by the same act nor installed (`absent`); installed but with a `manifest.version` outside the range (`out-of-range`); whose range is outside the stated grammar, whether or not the dependency is installed (`unreadable-range`, `latest` included); whose installed version is not `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` with optional leading `v` and `+build` (`unreadable-version`, a prerelease included); or whose `dependencies` is present but not a record (`unreadable-declaration`, pinned against the marketplace array shape). Every unmet entry of every delivered package is reported in one answer, in declaration order. Still passing: a package with no `dependencies` or an empty record (pinned in the protocol suite as "exactly as it installed before"); every entry installed inside its range; every entry delivered by the same artifact. Enablement is not judged, as ADR-0141 D2 says. The refusal envelope on the three HTTP doors is the one shape (`code`, `httpStatus` 422, `details` closed to `compatible`, `issues`, `unmet`); the runtime and cloud-connection suites assert the key set exactly, and the runtime suite parses the error with `ApiErrorSchema`, which the regenerated ledger makes pass.

Two consequences of fail-closed worth stating, both correct under the ADR and both documented on the new docs page, neither blocking: (i) `ManifestSchema.version` admits SemVer 2.0.0 prereleases, so an app installed at `6.1.0-beta.1` can never satisfy a dependent until a release version is installed; (ii) the `found` label has one mislabelled corner: a union whose first alternative admits `0.0.0` but not the installed version while another alternative is unreadable (e.g. `lt-5 || latest` against installed `7.0.0`) passes the `rangeReadable` probe and is then reported as `unreadable-version` naming a perfectly readable `7.0.0`. The install is still refused, so the accept set is right; only the fact row and its message misname the side. Worth a one-line fix in the D5 PR (probe the range with each alternative, or report `unreadable-range` when `admits` is null and the version read).

**B. Presence-only satisfaction by a composed app — right.** `delivered` ids and `deliveredIds` are collected into one set before any entry is judged, and `if (delivered.has(dependency)) continue` runs before the range is read, so an in-artifact entry is never judged for range (metadata-core test: `orders` declaring `^1.0.0` against a co-delivered `core` at `2.0.0` passes; the control without `core` is refused). Install-local judges `packages[].manifest` when `packages` is an array and the manifest itself otherwise, which is the same split `resolveArtifactPackageEntries` makes, so what is judged is what will register. One note: `deliveredIds: [manifestId]` also counts the artifact wrapper's id as delivered. In a `composeStacks(..., { manifest: 'preserve' })` artifact the wrapper id is one of the package ids, so the arm is redundant there; where a wrapper id names no package, a module declaring it passes at install but would be `absent` on a later standalone install. ADR-0141 D2 arm 2 speaks of "a package delivered by the same artifact", and the install-local ledger does record the artifact under `manifestId`, so the reading is defensible; noted, not a defect.

**C. D1 verdicts unchanged by the shared peel — right, by construction.** The three extracted helpers are byte-equivalent to the code they replace: `hyphenRangeEnds` keeps `split(/\s+-\s+/)` with the `length === 2` test; `peelComparatorOperator` keeps the same `startsWith` ladder and slices and the same `null` on no operator; `COMPARATOR_SEPARATOR` is the same `/[\s,]+/`; `MAX_RANGE_LENGTH` is the same 128. `alternativeAdmitsMajor` still reads `latest` as true and `comparatorAdmitsMajor` still returns `null` on an unparsed bound, so `assertProtocolCompat`'s admit-with-warning on `no-range` / `unparsed-range` and ADR-0087 D1's never-false-rejection contract are untouched. `protocol-handshake.test.ts` is not in the diff; the new suite cross-asserts `rangeAdmitsMajor('^6.2.0', 6)` true beside `rangeAdmitsVersion('^6.2.0', '6.1.0')` false, which is the one case the card exists for. The two readers share parsing and not policy: `rangeAdmitsVersion` returns `null` and each caller owns what `null` means.

**D. Fail-closed on an out-of-grammar range — right.** `readPartialVersion` returns `null` on anything that is not up to three dot-joined numeric or `x`/`X`/`*` parts, so `latest`, `next`, `~gt6.0`, `^6.0.0.1`, an empty alternative and a 200-char string all read `null` (pinned). `checkDeclaredDependencies` probes the range before looking at the registry, so an unreadable range is reported as such even when the dependency is absent (the author's fix is the range, not an install). The desugaring matches npm at exact-version granularity in every case I traced: caret on zero-major narrows to the first non-zero part (`^0.2.3`, `^0.0.3`, `^0.0`, `^0`), tilde pins the minor when written and the major otherwise, `gt` on a partial becomes `gte` the ceiling, `lte` on a partial becomes `lt` the ceiling, hyphen with a partial high end becomes `lt` its ceiling, `*`/`x` alone admits everything, a union admits when any alternative admits and is `null` only when none admits and one is unreadable (the same combination rule as `rangeAdmitsMajor`). The grammar the refusal prints (`DEPENDENCY_RANGE_GRAMMAR`) is the one the reader implements and the docs table repeats.

**E. The ledger row and the new metadata-core exports — right.** `DEPENDENCY_MISSING` sits under `@objectstack/metadata-core`, alphabetically first in that list, with no duplicate anywhere in the ledger at the head; its producer `DependencyMissingError` lives in that package, redeclares `code` as a literal and declares `status` and `statusCode` 422, the pattern `ProtocolIncompatibleError` in the same file already uses over `MetadataError(code, message)`, which is what `check:error-status-conformance` reads (green). The three reference pages regenerated from the ledger carry the new member (`+344 more`, the bullet in three lists); `packages/spec/api-surface/api.json` records that `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER` exists and not its members, so no api-surface regeneration is owed, and no other generated carrier of ledger codes exists (a sibling code appears at the head only in docs, changelogs, a release note and a hand-written QA checklist). The new public surface of `@objectstack/metadata-core`, through the existing `export * from './protocol-handshake.js'`: values `rangeAdmitsVersion`, `readExactVersion`, `DEPENDENCY_RANGE_GRAMMAR`, `checkDeclaredDependencies`, `assertDeclaredDependencies`, `DependencyMissingError`, `isDependencyMissingError`, `dependencyMissingAnswer`; types `ExactVersion`, `DependencyDeclaringManifest`, `InstalledDependencyRecord`, `UnmetDependency`, `DeclaredDependencyCheck`, `DependencyMissingIssue`, `DependencyMissingAnswer`. The changeset names the eight values; the types are the inputs and outputs of those values and need no separate line. `isDependencyMissingError` recognises by a `Symbol.for` brand, so the runtime door recognises an error thrown inside `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` (pinned by the lookalike test).

**F. The two out-of-surface files.** `scripts/docs-audit/handwritten-docs.json`: machine-required and nothing more. `check-audit-scope.mjs` derives the roster from the filesystem and exits 1 on any drift, so a new page under `content/docs/` cannot land without the entry; the one added line is the new page's path in sorted position. `scripts/adr-anchors/packages__metadata-core__src__protocol-handshake.ts.json`: right, and nothing more than an anchor, but "machine-required" overstates it. `check-adr-anchors.mjs` verifies the entries that exist (file present, ADR ids real, ids cited in the file); it does not demand an anchor for a newly governed file. Adding one is the convention its header states ("add one when an accepted ADR's decision is realized in code that would look arbitrary to someone reading the file alone"), which this file now is: fail-closed beside an admit-with-warning handshake is exactly the shape a reasonable engineer would "fix". The entry's shape matches its siblings (`file`, `adrs`, `invariant`), both ids it lists (ADR-0141, ADR-0087) appear in the file, and its invariant text restates D2 correctly. `check:adr-anchors` is green on the head.

**G. Claims I could not verify from the inputs.** The PR body's HotCRM paragraph (three modules declaring `'app.objectstack.hotcrm': '^6.0.0'` at `d91c7b0`) is outside this brief's inputs. What the code pins is that the claim follows if the manifests read as stated: a co-delivered app is presence-only, and `^6.0.0` admits `6.0.0`.

### ② Semver level

**Levels.** The changeset introduces `patch` on `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/cloud-connection` and `@objectstack/spec`, which are exactly the five published packages the diff moves (docs and `scripts/` publish nothing). Under AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist item 3 the level follows the `Metadata-protocol` kind alone: `none` takes `patch`, and "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition". The levels match. `Check Changeset` is green.

**The declaration line.** The dev's `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is the one AGENTS.md requires here, and the claim's `no (narrowing ...)` does not survive the diff. AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist item 3 fixes the syntax (`yes|no` plus at most one arm from the closed pair, `(narrowing)` is BREAKING, `no (widening)` malformed); the meaning is held by the one reader AGENTS.md's rule points at, `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`: the value answers 「本卡放宽接受集或扩大公开面吗」, and `yes (narrowing)` is "a diff that widens one surface and narrows another; both facts are true and both are read", while `no (narrowing)` is "NOT a widening, but breaking". `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` (ruling A) restates it: "`Clause-②` keeps its MEANING (does this diff widen or narrow a published accept set or public surface)". This diff adds a member to the closed `ApiErrorSchema.code` set through the ledger and eight value exports to `@objectstack/metadata-core`'s public surface, which is a widening of a published surface, and it narrows install acceptance, which is the `(narrowing)` arm. So `yes (narrowing)`. The claim line was written before the diff existed and reads the card's intent; the dev measured the diff, and the measurement governs. The PR body and the changeset both carry `yes (narrowing)` and agree. Served-tier is unaffected: the ledger file is a published schema, so the schema face already puts this review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` whatever the line reads.

**Metadata-protocol: `none` stands.** AGENTS.md item 3 defines the kind as "the change to what a metadata author can write": a new key, accepted value or type is `added`; "a key removed or tombstoned, a value refused or a requirement tightened is `narrowed`". `ManifestSchema.dependencies` is unchanged at `z.record(z.string(), z.string())`, its JSDoc already reads "Map of package IDs to version requirements" with a `^2.0.0` example, and every value it parsed before still parses, builds, validates and is stored by `PATCH`. What changes is the answer the install act gives against the environment, which ADR-0141 D2 places at the install doors and D8 fences off from the spec ("No spec shape changes in this record"). The borderline the dev names is real: an out-of-grammar range such as `latest` is refused at install whatever the environment holds, which reads like "a value refused". I rule it `none` because the refusal is at the install act and not at the authoring protocol, the grammar enforced is the one the key has always documented (a version requirement, not a dist-tag), and ADR-0141 merge question 6 pairs this backstop with the author-side `os lint` rule on the sibling card, where the authoring surface is stated. If the maintainer reads the `latest` refusal the other way, the correction is `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` with `minor` on at least one moved package, and nothing else in the record changes. Precedents #25954 and #25964 are cited by the dev and are outside this brief's inputs; this ruling rests on the AGENTS.md text alone.

**Carriers.** The changeset carries the `**BREAKING**` banner (signal 2 of `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`), the `(narrowing)` arm (signal 4) and exactly one ADR-0087 marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, with a "What changes for you" section; the summary line carries no `!` (signal 3), which the gate does not require when signals 2 and 4 are present. The disposition is right: no metadata key is added, removed, renamed or re-shaped, so `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing to rewrite and no tombstone is owed. The PR body's `Declarations` section repeats both lines with the same values.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Open question 6a (`PackageDependencySchema` with its `optional` arm) and 6b (`AppManifestSchema.dependencies`).** Neither is in this diff, and the PR is sound without them. D2 reads `ManifestSchema.dependencies` only; an array-shaped declaration is reported `unreadable-declaration` (pinned), so the marketplace shape cannot pass as "no dependencies"; and ADR-0141 D8 already fixes that `optional` has no record spelling and D2 never reads it, which this PR honours (every record entry required, no optional arm, D8 item 2 satisfied by construction). The dev's zero-reader measurement holds at the head: at `12daab9542`, `PackageDependencySchema`, `AppManifestSchema` and `versionRange` have no hit under `packages/`, `examples/` or `apps/` outside `packages/spec/`, and inside spec the hits are the two declaring files, their two tests, and `package-dependency-dual-source.test.ts`, which pins the #4741 rename and would need updating by a retirement PR (there is no `ui/` tree in this repo; the console is objectui and outside these inputs). Recommendation A for both (retire now, one spec PR with the retirement kit) is the contract-first answer and matches D8 item 3's "decided on a measured reader count". Escalated to the maintainer as the card asks; not a condition on this PR.

**Open question 3 (the declaration line).** Ruled above: keep `yes (narrowing)`. No edit owed.

**Dogfood failure `authz-probe-blind-spot`.** Verified: `packages/qa/dogfood/test/authz-probe-blind-spot.test.ts` (the dev's `test/...` path is relative to `packages/qa/dogfood`) and `packages/runtime/src/domains/i18n.ts` are byte-identical between `origin/main` (`05f7758f05`) and the head; `handleI18nRequest` occurs 4 times in `i18n.ts` on both. The head's CI dogfood check-runs are `skipped`, not red: `Dogfood Regression Gate (shard/3)` and `Dogfood Verify CLI` carry `if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' && != 'merge_group'` in `ci.yml`, so they never run on a PR event; the aggregator `Dogfood Regression Gate` runs `if: always()` and concluded `success` over skipped shards. The dev's full local dogfood is therefore the only measurement of that row, and its "red on main since #25956" attribution is outside these inputs; what this record can say is that this PR does not touch either file. Carrier stays as the dev filed it (noted, not filed).

**Deviations from the claim.** (1) The declaration line, ruled above. (2) Two files outside the claim's listed surface: the roster entry is machine-required; the anchor is convention-required and correct (① F). Neither is a `ui/**` edit or a spec key change, so neither is the stop-on-breach case the claim names.

**Out-of-scope findings and the split.** Items 4 and 5 (D5 co-owner source and rehydrate order) and First readings 2 and 6 are deferred to the next PR on #25792; the docs page says D5 is not delivered, and the Sharing-a-namespace section states today's `NAMESPACE_CONFLICT` behaviour correctly. The PR is `Part of`, the card stays open, and `Part-of PR must not also close its card` is green. Item 3 has no `ui/**` edit (verified: 18 files, none under `ui/`). Item 6 made no spec key change (the only `packages/spec/**` edit is the ledger row).

**Two non-blocking notes for the D5 PR**, from ① A and ① B: the `found` mislabel on a union with one unreadable alternative, and the artifact-wrapper id in `deliveredIds`.

**CI still owed at review time.** Test Core shards 1, 3, 4, 5, 7 and `Type Check · workspace` were in progress; every concluded run is green. Landing waits on them as it would for any PR; this record does not vouch for them.
